Step 6b complete. Report at `research/frontier-11-alpha-step6.md`, committed as `70f0b6e5`.

## Freeze verdict: text yes, artifacts no

**The item text is ready for the step-7 sweep. The proof contracts are not.**

## Two false claims found *after* the readers finished

**`thm-formal-composition-laws` asserted a false theorem.** Title and Statement both claimed *admissible* formal composition is associative. I verified the `formal-series` refuter's counterexample coefficientwise against the library's own definition: with `q = x−x²`, `w = q⟨−1⟩`, `h = 1+x`, all four compositions are admissible, yet `(w∘q)∘h = 1+x` while `w∘(q∘h) = −x`. Repaired with the zero-constant hypothesis on both inner series; the two facts citing it restated.

**`thm-alternating-conjugacy-class-splitting-criterion` was false for `n ≤ 1`**, where `A_n = S_n` and the index-2 hypothesis its `[F3]` instantiates fails. `n ≥ 2` added and propagated to four consumers.

## The three flagged repairs

All three confirmed. The sparse-spikes case is decisive: the step-4 scaffold says verbatim *"Define the value at zero to be zero… nevertheless its derivative there equals the chosen value zero"* — the step-5 author deviated from its own scaffold, and the reader restored it.

## Where I was wrong, and where a reader was

I missed a defect in my own impact pass: `lem-cauchy-product-of-absolutely-convergent-complex-series` uses coordinate arithmetic and cites the definition the D12 rewrite moved it out of. The `complex` refuter caught it.

Reader-4's provenance upgrade on the one-point-space example was **right**, but its new locator was wrong — Riehl 2.1.6(ii) is the Sierpiński space representing the open-set functor. I fetched the PDF, corrected it to 2.1.5(ii), and swept all 30 Riehl/Leinster locators in that batch, finding one more stale one.

## What blocks the artifacts

Six refuters and reader-5 independently found proof-contract rows that are **false of the text they certify** — invented boundary evidence, `iff` rows marked `not_applicable` on genuine biconditionals, quotes truncated before the supporting clause — while `proof-contract --strict` reports 206/206 and 0 errors. It checks substring existence, not support. §6 specifies an artifact-only Beta round, with the hard condition that no item may be touched: a contract row that can't be made true without editing a proof is a new mathematical finding, not a formatting fix.

**150 `risk_review` records written** (`--require-reviewed` passes for the first time this run). **Impact re-measured** against fresh snapshots — the orchestrator's `probe-post-step6` was stamped before the readers finished, so I re-took it: of 3,482 pre-existing items exactly 4 changed, and their 40-item cone is dispositioned. Two published-side citation repairs are owed but blocked until step 10; both need an owner decision.
